listBibl.bibl: Felix Liebermann, Die Gesetze der Angelsachsen, vol. 1 (Halle: Niemeyer, 1903), p. 624

An English crib of the Latin text, semi-literal, made for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model (LLM) made by Anthropic. It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: Ps Cn for 26
div.ab: Episcopi, abbates et barones mei non calumniabuntur pro uenatione, si non regales feras occiderint; et si regales, restabunt rei regi pro libito suo, sine certa emendatione.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 624 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: My bishops, abbots and barons shall not be accused for hunting, if they have not killed royal beasts; and if [they kill] royal ones, they shall remain liable to the king at his pleasure, without fixed compensation.
